rules.name: Statement
rules.text: The voice falls at the end. The last syllable of the group is a little higher and longer before it falls.

rules.name: Question-word question
rules.text: The voice usually falls at the end, as in a statement. Questions with qui, que, quand, où, comment, combien, pourquoi, quel. With a gentle rise instead, they sound extra friendly.

rules.name: Yes/no question
rules.text: Often the same words as a statement: only the melody makes it a question (Vous venez du Portugal?). The voice rises at the end. With est-ce que or inversion it rises too.

rules.name: Echo question
rules.text: The voice rises high at the end. You're surprised or checking what you heard. French often starts it with Quoi or Comment, or just repeats the words.

rules.name: Exclamation
rules.text: The stressed word goes very high, then the voice falls a long way. Feeling: joy, anger, surprise.

rules.name: List
rules.text: On each item the voice rises a little → until the list is finished. Then it falls ↘.

rules.name: Polite request
rules.text: A polite request is often a statement with je voudrais (the voice falls), or a question with pourriez-vous (the voice rises gently). s'il vous plaît and a friendly tone do the rest.
